criteria.note: CONJUNCTION: net mean > +0.10R with clustered t > 2 AND excess > 0 with clustered t > 2, plus n/concentration/year/NO_BASELINE vetoes. Year-bucketing is a veto, not 24 independent significance tests. See BLUEPRINT.md §7.2.1.
criteria.amendedAt: G0 Amendment 3, 2026-10-27, before any claim result

placebo.note: A real CONFIRMED count must exceed p95FakeConfirms to be credible.

sensitivityRule.valSupportCriterion: The claim's VAL-window cell must independently reach CONFIRMED under the SAME frozen CLAIM_CRITERIA as amended at G0 Amendment 3 (net mean > +0.10R with day-clustered t > 2, AND excess over matched random > 0 with day-clustered t > 2, AND all vetoes clear), evaluated once, with the VAL role spent on promotion.
sensitivityRule.amendedAt: G0 Amendment 2, 2026-10-27, before any claim result

evidence.testOrder: EXPLICIT FROZEN SEQUENCE (v1.3, byte-identical to v1.2). evidenceTier is a diagnostic rank, NOT an ordering key and NOT an evidence claim.

grades.PEER_REVIEWED_TEST: at least one empirical study tests this family; URL opened 2026-10-27
grades.PRACTITIONER_ONLY: no empirical study found; claim rests on practitioner literature only

channel-breakout.citation: Brock, W., Lakonishok, J. & LeBaron, B. (1992). Simple Technical Trading Rules and the Stochastic Properties of Stock Returns. Journal of Finance 47(5), 1731-1764.
channel-breakout.tests: trading range break (channel/resistance-support breakout) rules on DJIA 1897-1986
channel-breakout.finding: in-sample support; later work (Sullivan, Timmermann & White 1999) warns of data-snooping

ma-cross.citation: Chong, T.T.-L. & Ng, W.-K. (2008). Technical analysis and the London stock exchange: testing the MACD and RSI rules using the FT30. Applied Economics Letters 15(14), 1111-1114. DOI 10.1080/13504850600993598.
ma-cross.tests: MACD (exponential moving-average crossover) rule on 60 years of FT30
ma-cross.finding: MACD/RSI beat buy-and-hold in most cases (positive, single-market study)

opening-range.citation: Holmberg, U., Lönnbark, C. & Lundström, C. (2013). Assessing the profitability of intraday opening range breakout strategies. Finance Research Letters 10(1), 47-53. DOI 10.1016/j.frl.2012.09.001.
opening-range.tests: opening-range breakout on US crude-oil futures, bootstrap test
opening-range.finding: full-sample success is NOT robust across three sub-periods (mixed/negative)

level-retest.citation: Osler, C. L. (2000). Support for Resistance: Technical Analysis and Intraday Exchange Rates. FRBNY Economic Policy Review 6(2), 53-68.
level-retest.tests: support/resistance (level) signals from six FX firms, intraday 1996-1998
level-retest.finding: levels predict intraday trend interruptions, but firms mis-rank level strength

osc-fade.citation: Chong, T.T.-L., Ng, W.-K. & Liew, V.K.-S. (2014). Revisiting the Performance of MACD and RSI Oscillators. Journal of Risk and Financial Management 7(1), 1-12 / MPRA Paper 54149.
osc-fade.tests: RSI(14,30/70) and RSI(21,50) oscillator rules on five OECD indices 1976-2002
osc-fade.finding: RSI(14,30/70) profitable on DJIA but not consistently across markets

band-reversion.citation: Lento, C., Gradojevic, N. & Wright, C. S. (2007). Investment information content in Bollinger Bands? Applied Financial Economics Letters 3(4), 263-267. DOI 10.1080/17446540701206576.
band-reversion.tests: Bollinger Band (20,2) and variants, four markets 1995-2004, transaction costs
band-reversion.finding: BB underperform buy-and-hold; contrarian inversion does better (negative for the textbook fade)

candlestick-reversal.citation: Marshall, B. R., Young, M. R. & Rose, L. C. (2006). Candlestick technical trading strategies: Can they create value for investors? Journal of Banking & Finance 30(8), 2303-2323. DOI 10.1016/j.jbankfin.2005.08.001.
candlestick-reversal.tests: 26 candlestick reversal patterns on DJIA component stocks 1992-2002, bootstrap
candlestick-reversal.finding: no value; neither bullish nor bearish signals beat buy-and-hold (negative)

vol-compression.citation: Crabel, T. (1990). Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns & Opening Range Breakout (Traders Press) — practitioner book, not a peer-reviewed test.
vol-compression.tests: NR7 / inside-bar / volatility-contraction patterns — NO academic test found
vol-compression.finding: practitioner only. Holmberg et al. (2013) discusses Crabel's contraction-expansion principle but tests ORB, not NR7/inside-bar. This is the PLAINLY WRONG item: v1.2 ranked this family tier 1 with no empirical study.

evidence.note: Each family has one opened empirical study or is marked PRACTITIONER_ONLY. Full URLs above. No outcomes from our own data were used.

note: DRY RUN: synthetic trades only. No ledger records written. This calibrates the harness (kill criterion #7).
baselineMode: UNCONTROLLED synthetic calibration (no baseline object). Amendment 3: verifyReal() REFUSES this mode and requires random-baseline.json; every real row is NO_BASELINE-guarded.
